findings.claim: The proposal makes embedded SurrealKV a `Store` implementation but defines no process-ownership or lock model, while R12 detach, a long-lived `c3-mcp` server and a foreground CLI can all touch one repository's DB at the same time; embedded SurrealKV is opened as a single-process on-disk engine, so concurrent C3 processes on one repo have undefined behaviour (open failure, blocking, or corruption of the index).

findings.trigger: The first ~50 consultations on a repo, or any period where a reviewer is repeatedly drawn onto hard briefs.

evidence.observation: Posterior width exceeds the between-reviewer gap, so Thompson's exploration is indistinguishable from noise while still being recorded as a routing decision.

reviewer_checks.note: Corroborate sparse/delayed labels and incomplete replay inputs. Contradict median n<20 as a proof of unsoundness or non-identifiability; no universal threshold follows. Selection constraints and reward definitions require evaluation.

findings.claim: The reply schema is closed (`additionalProperties:false`, `schema_version` enum `["1"]`, `evidence.kind` enum of four values), so a pack-only `http` reviewer has no honest way to say 'this file was in my slice': it must either claim `read-code` (which today implies it read the repo) or downgrade to `inferred`, and any C3-side addition (pack hash, routing, needs[]) requires a coordinated schema bump with the plugin that still validates "1".

findings.claim: Porting the xelth.rs retriever shape drags in the embedding stack (candle, hf-hub, tokenizers, a 768-dim model download on first run) and its silent failure mode, which contradicts 'one static binary', offline use, and instant context assembly; the retrieval floor that actually needs no vectors is BM25 plus the three-layer graph.

candle-core/nn/transformers 0.10, hf-hub, tokenizers, plus `[profile.dev.package."*"].opt-level=3` because debug Candle inference is 20-100x slower.
`[dependencies] # Deliberately none yet` and `[profile.release] lto=true, strip=true` — the current binary-size discipline the ML stack would end.

findings.claim: `http` engines are stateless, so the plugin's timeout recovery ('one continuation turn on the same thread') and the 'never fork/resume across lineages' rule have no substrate; without deciding thread identity, sent-context identity and lineage naming for OpenRouter now, continuation, resume commands and dedup across waves will be retrofitted against a ledger that already stored the wrong keys.

`const API_BASE: &str = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"` with `chat/completions` — a stateless one-shot call, no thread/session id.
'one call, same reply schema' — no continuation or resume story for the http path.

findings.remedy: Define `lineage = provider::model::endpoint` with `endpoint = openrouter/<model>`; treat `http` threads as C3-owned: persist the sent pack (hash + served paths) and the reply, so a continuation re-sends the recorded pack plus the partial answer instead of resuming a server-side thread. Mark `resume_supported: false` in the ledger so the CLI prints a re-run command rather than a resume command.

reviewer_checks.note: Corroborate the identity and retry specification gap. HTTP can use client-owned transcript identity; retries must preserve consultation and pack identity independently of provider thread support.

findings.claim: R17 is left contradictory (opt-in decided in the plugin, ON-by-default in C3's README) and the new probabilistic router makes it load-bearing: if routing quality is ever argued from telemetry rather than from the local index, the privacy terms and the participation policy become coupled and both get harder to change.
findings.trigger: Shipping C3 0.x with the README's ON-by-default text while the plugin documents opt-in, or proposing to seed new-installation priors from T-hub aggregates.

evidence.observation: R17 'decided opt-in on 2026-09-26 in the plugin ROADMAP — while C3's README says ON by default … This contradiction is open.'
'## Telemetry (on by default, off with one line)' with `CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY=off`, `--complain`, `--forget-me`.
T-hub rules: payload never includes task names, prompts, briefs, paths, thread ids or finding text — so topic tags for routing cannot be sent.

findings.verification: Diff the plugin ROADMAP R17 wording against C3 README's telemetry section and check whether any routing input could only come from the server side.
findings.remedy: Resolve R17 explicitly in the framing document, and state the invariant that keeps it cheap: all learning inputs (briefs, findings, marks, priors) stay local in the index; telemetry carries only aggregate counters. Then ON-by-default is defensible and independent of the router.

reviewer_checks.note: Corroborated consent contradiction. Server-derived routing priors are only hypothetical: the brief does not require them. Keep local learning independent of outbound telemetry.

findings.claim: Putting `finish_task` into `c3-mcp` imports eckSnapshot's writer behaviour (`git add .` + commit + delta snapshot) into a bridge whose entire trust posture is read-only reviewers and files-as-evidence, and C3's own AGENTS.md currently grants `"*": allow` with `model: GLM-4.7`, so the boundary is undocumented as well as unenforced.
findings.trigger: An agent calls the C3 MCP `finish_task` tool during or right after a consultation, committing review artifacts together with unrelated working-tree changes.

evidence.observation: Finish loop: 'write `.eck/lastsnapshot/AnswerToSA.md` → `git add .` + commit → `eck_update_auto` delta snapshot … prepends to JOURNAL.md'.
`c3-mcp` (stdio MCP: consult, panel, findings, snapshot, explain, finish_task) — finish_task listed alongside read/record tools.
Frontmatter: `model: GLM-4.7`, `permission: read/edit/bash/"*": allow` — no read-only posture for this repo.
`eck-core` MCP server points at `C:\Users\Dmytro\eckSnapshot\scripts\mcp-eck-core.js` — an absolute, machine-specific path, contrary to R13 host invariance.

findings.verification: List the MCP tools C3 intends to expose and classify each as read / record / writer; check whether any writer can be invoked without a separate permission gate.
findings.remedy: Keep `c3-mcp` to read + record tools (consult, panel status, findings, snapshot, explain). If `finish_task` is wanted, expose it as an explicitly-writer tool that never runs `git add .` (stage only the paths it wrote), and record the commit sha in the ledger. Replace the absolute `.mcp.json` path with a resolvable one per R13.

reviewer_checks.note: Corroborated as a writer-capability boundary requiring a decision: the eckSnapshot digest describes git add . and commit. Read-only reviewers do not require the entire coordinator to be read-only, and AGENTS.md text alone is not runtime enforcement.

findings.claim: Ten crates is premature for a binary that today has no dependencies and only `--version`/`--help`; crate boundaries drawn before the second implementation exists tend to freeze the wrong seams, and a `heavy` feature that gates individual call sites will leak `cfg` branches everywhere.
findings.trigger: Steps 1-3 of the port order (providers, one consultation, ledger/findings) needing cross-crate changes for a single behaviour fix.

evidence.observation: Entire current implementation: `--version`, `--help`, unknown-arg exit 2.
Single package, single `[[bin]]`, `[dependencies] # Deliberately none yet`.
Proposed workspace: c3-core, c3-store, c3-engines, c3-snapshot, c3-context, c3-panel, c3-telemetry, c3-mcp, c3-cli.

findings.verification: Sketch steps 1-3 of the port order against both layouts and count how many crate boundaries a single ledger-format change crosses.
findings.remedy: Start with `c3-core`, `c3-engines`, `c3-cli` as modules in one crate if needed; promote to crates when a second impl or a compile-time reason appears. Drop `c3-store` per finding #3. Put `surrealdb` behind a default-on `heavy` feature that gates whole modules (`Index: none` when off), never individual call sites.

reviewer_checks.note: Corroborate premature boundary freezing from Cargo.toml and src/main.rs. The proposal actually names nine crates, not ten; cross-crate churn and cfg proliferation are risks, not observed defects.

findings.claim: R17 telemetry consent is contradictory: plugin decided opt-in on 2026-09-26 while C3 README states ON-by-default. Shipping either without an explicit decision breaks trust and blocks acceptance.
findings.trigger: First run with default env (no CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY set) sends or withholds the per-consultation event.

evidence.observation: C3 README declares telemetry ON by default with one-line off switch and first-run notice.
Digest records plugin R17 as decided opt-in on 2026-09-26 and flags the contradiction with C3 README as open.

findings.verification: Read README telemetry section against plugin ROADMAP R17 note and observe first-run/dry-run notice behavior.
findings.remedy: Decide once, in writing, before Store/Engine traits freeze: either reconcile to opt-in everywhere or document why C3 diverges; gate first telemetry send on that decision.

reviewer_checks.note: Corroborated; same unresolved R17 contradiction. This framing can receive advice, but implementation needs one documented default.

findings.claim: "DB rebuildable, losing it loses no evidence" is false for the proposed memory: participation priors, reviewer history and graph edges derived from past briefs live only in SurrealDB and are not reconstructible from files+repo alone.
findings.trigger: Delete SurrealKV directory and re-run selection or retrieval on an existing task.

evidence.observation: Proposed shape point 2 says DB is index+memory (scoreboard, priors, code graph, cross-project history) yet rebuildable from files+repo.
Plugin scoreboard today feeds nothing back; R15 plans weighted draw from usefulness+topic, i.e. new state with no file format defined.

findings.verification: Delete the DB dir on a fixture task, rebuild, and diff subsequent panel draw and retrieve_context output vs pre-delete.
findings.remedy: Define the rebuild contract explicitly: either persist routing state (marks, probabilities, seed, brief embeddings) as files and treat DB as pure cache, or admit DB holds durable memory and specify backup/export/corruption recovery.

reviewer_checks.note: Contradict the categorical claim that these values necessarily live only in the DB: the brief declares them rebuildable, and the plugin retains briefs, ratings and outcomes. The real open requirement is preserving all source evidence, historical versions and routing inputs, particularly across projects.

findings.claim: Thompson sampling over per-(member,purpose,topic) Beta posteriors is unsound at tens of consultations: posteriors stay prior-dominated, similarity-weighted slicing makes samples thinner, and the draw will look arbitrary while claiming to be telemetry-driven.
findings.trigger: Early life (fewer than ~50 rated consultations) or a novel topic with no similar stored briefs.

evidence.observation: Brief proposes Beta posterior + Thompson sampling with epsilon floor and neutral prior, similarity via BM25/HNSW over stored briefs.
Scoreboard has only CONSULTS/USABLE/HIT%=verified/(verified+rejected) with no aggregate usefulness formula; R15 has zero code.

findings.verification: Simulate draws on a tens-of-rows scoreboard fixture; check selection entropy and sensitivity to one Y/P/N mark.
findings.remedy: Start with epsilon-greedy/softmax over a pooled hierarchical prior (global -> purpose -> topic override), log full posteriors; promote to Thompson only after a stated sample-size gate.

reviewer_checks.note: Corroborate uncertainty and sparse topic slices. Contradict the claim that prior-dominated Thompson sampling is inherently unsound; strong priors can be appropriate. Predictive usefulness and sensitivity remain untested.

findings.claim: Adding the OpenRouter http engine breaks the bridge's core invariant 'never handles a key': an env-var key plus error strings, spool, ledger and judge inputs become new exfiltration surfaces, and redact() coverage is load-bearing.
findings.trigger: Any failed http consultation (401/timeout/retry) that surfaces provider errors, usage payloads, or spooled events.

evidence.observation: Proposed API path keeps key as env var, never prints/stores it, redact() on every error string.
Plugin invariant: bridge never creates/prints/pastes a key; Muse refuses when META/MODEL_API_KEY set; xelth redact() strips key and sk-or-shaped tokens (unit-tested).

findings.verification: Fail an http seat with a poisoned error string containing a fake sk-or key; inspect reply file, ledger, spool and stderr for leaks.
findings.remedy: Treat http as a trust boundary: key only via env/process inheritance, deny-list key-shaped strings in ledger/spool/errors with tests, document subscription-vs-API billing guard parity.

reviewer_checks.note: Corroborated credential-contract divergence and the need for error/output redaction. An actual failed-request leak has not been demonstrated.

findings.claim: Porting the eckSnapshot shape verbatim ports its redaction gap: redaction exists only in createSnapshot's output path, not the shared builder, and telemetry posts AnswerToSA-derived content to a hardcoded endpoint.
findings.trigger: Delta snapshot or explainer pack over a tree where a secret appears only in a changed file.

evidence.observation: Digest notes redaction only in createSnapshot output path, skeletonizer depth-6 JSDoc bug, hardcoded telemetry endpoint with leak risk.
Proposed c3-snapshot lists discovery/filters/redaction/depth but does not say redaction is centralized and tested on every output path including delta and explainer pack.

findings.verification: Add a secret to one file after the anchor, render delta and explainer outputs, and grep for the raw secret.
findings.remedy: Put redaction as a mandatory last pass in the shared builder used by full, delta, explainer and http context paths, with fixture tests including secrets introduced only in deltas.

reviewer_checks.note: Corroborated from the eckSnapshot digest as a conditional porting risk. C3 should share export sanitization and use a typed telemetry allowlist; it has not implemented the inherited leak.

findings.claim: Lock model is underspecified once a DB exists: today the task lock plus detached status file serialize consultations, but embedded SurrealKV adds a second lock domain (index writes, concurrent panel members, two tools on one repo) with Windows path behavior unaddressed.
findings.trigger: Parallel panel members indexing while a second tool (plugin or C3) opens the same task/DB.

evidence.observation: R12 decisions: foreground writes starting, background holds .consult.lock, second consult on task blocks; no daemon/queue.
Q8 names lock model with DB present and Windows/macOS/Linux paths as expensive-to-change but proposal fixes Store/Engine traits in step 1 without fixing it.

findings.verification: Run two concurrent consultations on one task fixture and kill one mid-index; check lock release, status file state, and DB open after restart.
findings.remedy: Specify before step 1: single-writer rule for the DB, lock ordering (file lock then DB txn), stale-lock recovery, and path canonicalization per OS.

history.note: Claim confirmed by RC1: exclusive fail-fast open, no shared reader; adopted as D1/D11 in state.md and DESIGN.md section 7
history.evidence: RC1 harness (scratchpad rc1/skvtest, surrealdb 3.0.5 -> surrealkv 0.21.0, Windows 11, 2026-09-26): second process opening the same surrealkv dir fails at connect in ~10 ms with os error 33 (lock violation), no blocking, no reader mode; clean exit and taskkill /F both release the lock with data intact. Design rule D1/D11: only the task-lock holder opens the embedded index, others run Index: none; multi-process needs the ws:// server.

reviewer_checks.note: Corroborated missing lock/recovery design, including process ownership and path identity. Windows-specific failure behavior and kill recovery remain untested.

findings.claim: The proposed retrieval integration omits an embedding egress policy. Reusing xelth.rs's cloud embedding backend can send source snippets to Gemini during indexing, independently of an OpenRouter consultation or telemetry consent. Secret redaction does not make confidential source public.
findings.trigger: C3 indexes a private repository through the borrowed Gemini embedding backend before, or without, an HTTP review.

evidence.observation: The digest identifies cloud Gemini and local Candle embedding backends.
The indexer redacts a source snippet and passes it to the selected embedder.
GeminiEmbedder sends supplied text through llm::embed_text when a key is present.
The proposal specifies reviewer HTTP transport but does not specify authorization or destination policy for embedding requests.

findings.verification: Run a disposable indexer fixture containing a non-secret confidential marker against a recording embedding endpoint and determine whether indexing transmits it when external embeddings are disabled.
findings.remedy: Default indexing to local lexical/graph processing; configure cloud embedding egress separately, apply export exclusions before embedding, and record the embedding destination and model version.

findings.claim: Pack-only evidence can fit reply schema v1, but the proposal does not require retaining the exact sanitized pack, source mappings and coverage manifest. Without those artifacts, a later reader cannot establish what an HTTP reviewer actually saw or map transformed snippets back to the reviewed revision.
findings.trigger: A reviewer cites a truncated, skeletonized or redacted snippet, and the repository or index changes before the finding is audited.

evidence.observation: Evidence reference and observation are unrestricted strings. The schema does not require read-code to mean direct filesystem access.
The proposal promises deterministic assembly and the same reply schema but does not define retained request artifacts, source maps or coverage metadata.

findings.verification: Generate a pack from a dirty fixture repository, collect one cited finding, modify the source and rebuild the index; verify that the original citation can still be resolved entirely from retained consultation artifacts.
findings.remedy: Retain the sanitized pack and a versioned sidecar containing content hash, source revision/dirty hashes, source spans, omissions and transformation versions. Use existing evidence.reference strings to cite it; keep routing metadata outside the strict reply envelope unless a coordinated schema change is needed.

findings.claim: Porting xelth.rs's embedding failure behavior would admit nonsemantic vectors as successful embeddings, contaminating HNSW retrieval and any similarity-based routing. The defensible concern is invalid-vector fallback, not that a static executable inherently cannot use external model assets.
findings.trigger: An embedding key is absent, an embedding request fails, or indexing runs with embeddings skipped and subsequently includes those vectors in similarity search.

evidence.observation: Missing credentials and API failures return Ok(generate_mock_embedding(text)); the mock is a normalized pseudorandom vector derived from a text hash.
The implementation emits rate-limited warnings that mock similarity is meaningless, so describing this path as wholly silent is inaccurate.
Skipped embeddings and propagated embedding errors produce a constant 768-dimensional vector.

findings.verification: Index unrelated snippets with embeddings unavailable and inspect stored embedding status and retrieval results; confirm that fallback vectors are excluded from HNSW and routing.
findings.remedy: Represent unavailable embeddings explicitly, omit them from vector search, and fall back to BM25/graph retrieval with a recorded degradation reason. Version model, dimensions and preprocessing; evaluate dependency and model-asset costs separately.

findings.claim: An unconditional inclusion-probability floor epsilon per member is not always feasible when selecting exactly k reviewers. With N eligible members, N*epsilon must be at most k; purpose, budget and diversity restrictions can additionally make a member's inclusion impossible. The proposal does not define whether epsilon is a mixture share, a per-seat probability or a panel inclusion floor.
findings.trigger: A large roster is used for a one-seat shadow panel, or a member is excluded by purpose or budget while the policy still promises a positive floor.

evidence.observation: The policy combines k-or-budget selection, a per-member epsilon floor, purpose gates and lab diversity without defining their precedence.
The sum of member inclusion probabilities equals expected panel size k. Therefore N positive floors require N*epsilon <= k, and an infeasible member has inclusion probability zero.

findings.verification: Exercise the policy specification with k=1, N=20 and epsilon=0.1, then add a purpose-ineligible member; require either an explicit configuration rejection or a mathematically consistent interpretation.
findings.remedy: Define epsilon as an exploration mixture over feasible panels after eligibility filtering, distinguish inclusion probabilities from Thompson samples, and record constraint precedence and infeasibility outcomes.

ratings.note: Astra: separated EvidenceStore from ContextIndex, defined reward/replay requirements for routing, caught the embedding egress and mock-vector risks, and corroborated or corrected every prior finding with a reason
GLM: tight, on-target; schema byte-compat, .eck collision, reward-gap caveat, two runnable RCs
MiMo: two accurate reframes (cross-project rebuild, key-invariant wording) but invalid JSON, no machine findings, generic prose
Kimi k3: cheapest signal per token; surfaced defer-SurrealDB option and no-R15-oracle -> golden tests
Qwen: highest value; RecordStore/Index split, roster lab-field break, closed-schema evidence.kind gap, two grounded blockers, five RCs
Muse: strong framing (three trust models, sidecar/event-sourced) but findings duplicate others, R17 over-rated as blocker, inaccurate claim that priors live only in the DB
